Co sprawdzić przed wdrożeniem zmian?: What to check before rolling out changes?
Pierwszy krok to krótki audyt obecnego s: The first step is a short audit of the current state. You need to check whether the page headline clearly states the offer, whether the most important services are visible without searching, whether users understand the collaboration process and whether the form collects only the necessary data. It's also worth going through the website on a phone, because that's where most conversion problems appear: buttons that are too small, long sections, awkward form fields, heavy images or elements that only look good on desktop.
Drugi krok to sprawdzenie danych. Sama o: The second step is checking the data. The opinion that “the website doesn't work” alone is too imprecise. It's better to check which subpages get visits, where users leave, whether they click the CTA, whether they scroll to the form and whether form submission is tracked correctly in GA4, the Meta Pixel or another analytics system. Without this, it's easy to fix things that aren't the real cause of the problem.
Trzeci krok to priorytety. Nie każdą pop: The third step is priorities. Not every fix has to be made right away. It's worth first improving the places closest to the decision: the hero, the offer, the trust section, prices or scope, the form, the CTA and speed. Only later does it make sense to expand the blog, add extra animations, more advanced modules or new supporting subpages.

Phrases like “comprehensive service”, “an individual approach” and “high quality” aren't enough if they're not backed up by the scope, the process, examples and proof. Users must know what exactly they get, what the collaboration looks like, how many decisions will be on their side and what to expect after sending an inquiry.

If you don't measure phone clicks, form submissions, moves to the cart or important CTAs, you don't know whether a change actually helped. Decisions are then made based on impressions, not data. With advertising, this is especially risky, because the budget may be spent on traffic that never had a well-prepared conversion path.
